text:
The **University of the Andes (Colombia)** was founded in 1948 by Mario Laserna Pinzón amid a period of political change and economic modernization in Colombia, aiming to provide nonsectarian and non-politically affiliated higher education. Modeled after American universities, it sought to train professionals to support Colombia's industrial development and to cultivate national leadership. Starting with just 80 students, the university emphasized a broad liberal and technical education, developed early exchange programs with U.S. institutions, and maintained political neutrality despite rising national violence.
Legally established as a nonprofit in 1948 and granted university status in 1964, Universidad de los Andes is governed by a Board of Trustees, Board of Directors, and academic councils overseeing its 14 academic units including 10 faculties. The Bogotá main campus mixes renovated historical and modern buildings, featuring extensive academic and sports facilities. The university boasts high academic standards, with 95% of undergraduates from the top 1% of Colombian high schools, a faculty largely holding foreign PhDs, and broad international exchange programs with over 119 universities worldwide. Its mission centers on academic excellence, pluralism, and social responsibility, aiming to address Colombia’s developmental challenges. Notable alumni include former Colombian presidents, ministers, prominent academics, artists, and public figures.
